scientific_choice.name: Bounded Entropy-Moment Reconstruction
reason: C5Y's centered first water-content moment remains the smallest additional scalar shape state with an exact projected conservation balance.
C5Z rejected the all-layer cubic-theta map because that map is not realizability preserving; it did not reject the first moment itself.
C6A shows that moving algebraic interface variables without new subgrid information collapses to already-closed routes.

The next family therefore keeps the conservation-derived S,M state but places the hydraulic profile in a bounded dual variable whose inverse map enforces the constitutive saturation interval by construction.
The family is selected from a mathematical realizability principle and degree count, not by minimizing C5R/C5N/C5P response error.

rejected_as_next.reason: Potentially physical, but an interface-local conserved water state is not yet distinguishable from simply adding/refining ordinary layers; no independent minimality argument currently selects it.
Scientifically viable separate representation direction, but DYN0A-MECH3B does not yet supply a unique prospective adaptation law. It remains deferred rather than silently chosen.

bounded_dual_derivation.frozen_constitutive_interval: Se in [L,U] with L=0.02 and U=0.995 for C6C qualification
bounded_dual_derivation.dual_space: v_i belongs to the complete polynomial space P3: b0+b1*P1+b2*P2+b3*P3
bounded_dual_derivation.important_boundary: eta is an information-theoretic convex generator used to define a realizability-preserving dual coordinate. C6B makes no claim that it is the thermodynamic entropy of soil water.

constraints: one centered first water-content moment M_i
Darcy flux continuity at internal faces
two external hydraulic boundary conditions globally
why_cubic_dual_space_is_prospective.basis_independence: Degree <=3 is the unique four-dimensional polynomial space; Legendre coordinates are numerical conditioning/basis choices, not a fitted physical order.

maximum_entropy_connection.statement: With only mean occupancy and first spatial moment constrained, maximizing binary information entropy yields an affine entropy-dual profile v=a0+a1*xi. This supplies the response-free realizability rationale for the dual coordinate.
maximum_entropy_connection.hydraulic_extension: The P2/P3 dual modes are not claimed to be extra maximum-entropy moments. They are the minimum additional algebraic degrees required by the already-frozen hydraulic interface and boundary constraints while staying inside the same realizability-preserving dual space.

literature.citation: Levermore, C.D. (1996), Moment closure hierarchies for kinetic theories, Journal of Statistical Physics 83, 1021-1065.
literature.relevance: Entropy-based moment closures provide a systematic way to reconstruct admissible distributions from a finite moment set.

literature.citation: Cernohorsky, J. and Bludman, S.A. (1994), Maximum Entropy Distribution and Closure for Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac Radiation Transport, Astrophysical Journal 433, 250-255.
literature.relevance: For a bounded occupancy field, the maximum-entropy dual has logistic/Fermi-Dirac form and respects lower and upper occupancy bounds. C6B uses only this mathematical bounded-realizability property, not the radiation physics.

literature.citation: Wu, X., Cheng, J., Shu, C.-W. (2026), A high-order bound-preserving finite difference multi-resolution WENO method for high-dimensional Richards equation, Advances in Water Resources 213, 105324.
literature.relevance: Independent Richards-equation evidence that preserving physical moisture bounds is a structural numerical requirement rather than a cosmetic post-processing step.

distinction_from_C5Z.structural_difference: C5Z approximates theta directly by a cubic polynomial, which can leave the admissible interval. BEMR approximates the unconstrained entropy-dual v and maps through a fixed sigmoid into the frozen Se interval, so realizability is structural for every finite coefficient vector.
distinction_from_C5Z.not_a_C5Z_retune: No C5Z coefficient, moment amplitude, polynomial order, constitutive limit, solver tolerance or hydrological residual is reused to tune BEMR.

exact_state_relations.note: C6B changes only the algebraic profile map from (S,M) to hydraulic subgrid structure. It does not change the exact projected moment balance.

realizability_domain.exact_first_moment_bound: Let Se_bar be the layer mean. Then |M| <= 0.5*DeltaTheta*d^2*((Se_bar-L)*(U-Se_bar)/(U-L)).
realizability_domain.derivation: After y=(Se-L)/(U-L), the extremal bounded profile is the edge-filled step and has |(1/2) integral xi*y dxi|=y_bar*(1-y_bar).
realizability_domain.requirement: C6C must check the unchanged C5Z target S,M states against this stricter BEMR constitutive-domain realizability bound before solving.

constraints: Use exactly the C5Z D8_B2P5 and D12_B2P5 partitions, seven mean-Se profiles, six moment patterns and two boundary cases.
Do not narrow the moment amplitudes after C5Z.
Use the same frozen B14 constitutive law and Se qualification interval [0.02,0.995].
All layers remain moment-enriched; no localization.
No clipping, limiting, coefficient regularization or response-based parameter.
Preregister quadrature, starts, solver tolerances, state residual scales and branch-agreement gates before execution.
No hydrological trajectory may be read or generated.
If C6C fails existence, uniqueness, state recovery or hydraulic continuity, stop BEMR without tuning the dual order, bounds, starts or state domain.
